hint: If the owner was present, nothing is paid; if it was hired, the hire covers it.

notes.text: μισθωτός, hired, an hireling, for the Hebrew śākîr.

greek: Ἐὰν δὲ ἀπατήσῃ τις παρθένον ἀμνήστευτον καὶ κοιμηθῇ μετʼ αὐτῆς, φερνῇ φερνιεῖ αὐτὴν αὐτῷ γυναῖκα.
hint: A man who seduces an unbetrothed virgin must pay her bride-price and take her as his wife.

With a dowry he will endow, the noun with its verb, for the Hebrew māhōr yimhārennâ; φερνίζω, not in Middle Liddell, LSJ's portion, endow, citing this verse.

reading: [[if haply|if haply, if|ἐάν]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[may cheat|may cheat and trick and outwit and beguile, may deceive|ἀπατάω]] [[any one|any one, some one, many a one, each one, every man|τις]] [[a maid|a maid and maiden and virgin and girl|παρθένος]] [[unwooed|unwooed and not sought in lawful wedlock|ἀμνήστευτος]] and [[may be lulled|may be lulled, may be hushed to sleep and put to sleep, may be lulled to rest and stilled and calmed, may fall asleep, may go abed and lie abed, may sleep, may fall asleep and die, may keep watch at night|κοιμάω]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] of her, [[to that which is brought by the wife|to that which is brought by the wife, to a dowry and portion, to a dower, to bridal gifts|φερνή]] [[will portion|will portion and endow|φερνίζω]] her to him [[a woman|a woman, a mistress and lady, a wife and spouse, a mortal woman|γυνή]].

hint: If her father refuses, the man pays silver equal to a virgin's bride-price.

notes.text: Throwing back his head he may throw it back, the participle with its own verb, for the Hebrew mā'ēn yĕmāʾēn.
According to as much as, ὅσον accusative after κατά.

greek: φαρμακοὺς οὐ περιποιήσετε. —
hint: Sorcerers are not to be kept alive.

notes.text: Poisoners, sorcerers, masculine plural: the Hebrew has mĕkaššēpâ, a sorceress, singular.
περιποιέω, to keep, save for oneself, for the Hebrew lōʾ tĕḥayyeh, you shall not let live.

reading: [[poisoners|poisoners and sorcerers and magicians, ones who are sacrificed as an atonement, scape-goats|φαρμακός]] not [[you will keep|you will keep and save for yourselves, you will compass and acquire and obtain, you will make gain|περιποιέω]]. —

greek: πᾶν κοιμώμενον μετὰ κτήνους, θανάτῳ ἀποκτενεῖτε αὐτούς. —
hint: Anyone who lies with an animal is to be put to death.

notes.text: Every thing lying, the neuter, read as a nominative standing first, taken up by αὐτούς.
You will kill them, plural: the Hebrew has môt yûmāt, he shall surely die.

reading: [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[being lulled|being lulled, being hushed to sleep and put to sleep, being lulled to rest and stilled and calmed, falling asleep, going abed and lying abed, sleeping, falling asleep and dying, keeping watch at night|κοιμάω]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] [[of flock and herd|of flock and herd, of a single beast, of a beast for riding|κτῆνος]], [[to death|to death, to the death threatened, to the sentence of death|θάνατος]] [[you will kill|you will kill and slay, you will condemn to death|ἀποκτείνω]] them. —

greek: ὁ θυσιάζων θεοῖς θανάτῳ ὀλεθρευθήσεται πλὴν κυρίῳ μόνῳ.
hint: Sacrificing to gods other than the lord alone brings utter destruction.

notes.text: πλήν before a dative is the conjunction, but, except, not the preposition, which takes the genitive.
θυσιάζω, to sacrifice, and ὀλεθρεύω, to destroy utterly, one translation each, plain text.

reading: the one sacrificing [[to gods|to gods, to the gods, to goddesses|θεός]] [[to death|to death, to the death threatened, to the sentence of death|θάνατος]] will be destroyed utterly [[but|but, than, much like, only not, except that, save that, except, save so far as, more than, save and short of|πλήν]] [[to lord|to lord, to master, to the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] [[to alone|to alone, to left alone and forsaken and solitary, to only|μόνος]].

greek: Καὶ προσήλυτον οὐ κακώσετε οὐδὲ μὴ θλίψητε αὐτόν· ἦτε γὰρ προσήλυτοι ἐν γῇ Αἰγύπτῳ. —
hint: The resident stranger is not to be wronged or oppressed, since Israel was a stranger in Egypt.

notes.text: You were, the imperfect of εἰμί, with the formula, as ἦσαν at 1:5.
προσήλυτος, one that has arrived, a sojourner, for the Hebrew gēr.

reading: And [[one that has arrived at|one that has arrived at, a sojourner, one who has come over to Judaism and a convert and proselyte|προσήλυτος]] not [[you will treat ill|you will treat ill and maltreat and afflict and distress, you will spoil and ruin, you will suffer ill and be in ill plight and be distressed|κακόω]] [[but not|but not, and not, nor, not even, not at all|οὐδέ]] [[not|not, that not, perhaps, surely not and you don't mean to say that|μή]] [[you may press|you may press and squeeze and pinch, you may pinch and compress and straiten, you may oppress and afflict and distress|θλίβω]] him; were, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]], [[ones that have arrived at|ones that have arrived at, sojourners, ones who have come over to Judaism and converts and proselytes|προσήλυτος]] [[in earth|within, inside of, and by means of earth, land, ground|ἐν; γῆ]] to [[name:Αἰγύπτῳ]]. —

names.gloss: (Αἴγυπτος, the Greek name of the land; Hebrew Miṣrayim)

greek: πᾶσαν χήραν καὶ ὀρφανὸν οὐ κακώσετε·
hint: No widow or orphan is to be mistreated.

notes.text: χήρα, bereft of a husband, a widow, coded as the adjective, as at Genesis 38:11.

reading: [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[bereft of a husband|bereft of a husband and a widow|χήρα]] and [[an orphan|an orphan, orphan and without parents and fatherless, bereaved, bereft, reft|ὀρφανός]] not [[you will treat ill|you will treat ill and maltreat and afflict and distress, you will spoil and ruin, you will suffer ill and be in ill plight and be distressed|κακόω]];

greek: ἐὰν δὲ κακίᾳ κακώσητε αὐτοὺς καὶ κεκράξαντες καταβοήσωσι πρός με, ἀκοῇ εἰσακούσομαι τῆς φωνῆς αὐτῶν
hint: If they are wronged and cry out to the lord, he will surely hear them.

notes.text: With badness you may treat ill, the noun with its verb's root, for the Hebrew ʿannēh tĕʿanneh.
With hearing I will hearken, for the Hebrew šāmōaʿ ʾešmaʿ.

greek: καὶ ὀργισθήσομαι θυμῷ καὶ ἀποκτενῶ ὑμᾶς μαχαίρᾳ, καὶ ἔσονται αἱ γυναῖκες ὑμῶν χῆραι καὶ τὰ παιδία ὑμῶν ὀρφανά. —
hint: The lord's anger will kill the oppressors, leaving their own wives widows and children orphans.

notes.text: I will be made angry with soul, θυμός, for the Hebrew wĕḥārâ ʾappî, and my anger will burn.

reading: and [[I will be made angry|I will be made angry and provoked to anger and irritated, I will grow angry and be wroth|ὀργίζω]] [[to soul|to soul, to spirit and heart, to anger and wrath, to mind and temper, to will and desire, to courage and spirit|θυμός]] and [[I will kill|I will kill and slay, I will condemn to death|ἀποκτείνω]] you [[to a large knife|to a large knife and dirk, to a knife for cutting up, to a short sword and dagger, to a sabre and bent sword, to a rasor|μάχαιρα]], and will be [[the women|the women, the mistresses and ladies, the wives and spouses, the mortal women|γυνή]] of you [[bereft of a husband|bereft of a husband and widows|χήρα]] and [[the young children|the young children, the young slave-lads|παιδίον]] of you [[orphan|orphan and without parents and fatherless, orphans, bereaved, bereft, reft|ὀρφανός]]. —

greek: ἐὰν δὲ ἀργύριον ἐκδανείσῃς τῷ ἀδελφῷ τῷ πενιχρῷ παρὰ σοί, οὐκ ἔσῃ αὐτὸν κατεπείγων, οὐκ ἐπιθήσεις αὐτῷ τόκον.
hint: Money lent to a poor brother is not to be pressed for or charged with interest.

notes.text: ἐκδανείζω, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's lend out at interest, one translation, plain text.

greek: ἐὰν δὲ ἐνεχύρασμα ἐνεχυράσῃς τὸ ἱμάτιον τοῦ πλησίον, πρὸ δυσμῶν ἡλίου ἀποδώσεις αὐτῷ·

hint: It is his only covering; if he cries out, the lord will hear, for he is merciful.

notes.text: Of his want of form, ἀσχημοσύνη, for the Hebrew lĕʿōrô, for his skin.
In what, the interrogative, plain text.

[[if haply|if haply, if|ἐάν]] [[really|really, at all events, surely, so, then and therefore|οὖν]] [[may cry down|may cry down and cry out against, may bawl down and outcry|καταβοάω]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] me, [[I will hearken|I will hearken and give ear to, I will hear, I will hearken to and give heed to|εἰσακούω]] of him; [[pitiful|pitiful and merciful and compassionate|ἐλεήμων]] [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]], am. —

greek: θεοὺς οὐ κακολογήσεις καὶ ἄρχοντας τοῦ λαοῦ σου οὐ κακῶς ἐρεῖς. —
hint: Neither the gods nor the rulers of the people are to be reviled.

notes.text: Gods, plural: the Hebrew has ʾĕlōhîm, which may be God or judges; the Greek's plural reads it as gods.
κακῶς, the adverb, filed inside κακός, as καλῶς is inside καλός: ill, evil.

reading: [[gods|gods, the gods, goddesses|θεός]] not [[you will speak ill of|you will speak ill of and revile and abuse|κακολογέω]] and [[rulers|rulers and commanders and chiefs and captains, chief magistrates|ἄρχων]] [[of the people|of the people, of the men, of the soldiers, of the land-army, of the common men, of the folk, of the Jews, of the Christians|λαός]] of you not [[ill|ill, evil|κακῶς]] [[you will say|you will say, you will speak, you will declare, you will call by name, you will tell|λέγω]]. —

greek: ἀπαρχὰς ἅλωνος καὶ ληνοῦ σου οὐ καθυστερήσεις· τὰ πρωτότοκα τῶν υἱῶν σου δώσεις ἐμοί.
hint: First-fruits of grain and wine are not to be held back, and the firstborn sons belong to the lord.

notes.text: First-fruits of threshing-floor and vat: the Hebrew has mĕlēʾātĕkā wĕdimʿăkā, your fullness and your juice.
πρωτότοκος, first-born, one translation, plain text.

reading: [[beginnings of a sacrifice|beginnings of a sacrifice and primal offerings, firstlings, first-fruits|ἀπαρχή]] [[of a threshing-floor|of a threshing-floor, of disk|ἅλων]] and [[of a tub|of a tub, of a wine-vat, of a trough|ληνός]] of you not [[you will come far behind|you will come far behind, you will be behind-hand|καθυστερέω]]; the first-born of the sons of you [[you will give|you will give, you will grant, you will provide, you will give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] to me.

greek: οὕτως ποιήσεις τὸν μόσχον σου καὶ τὸ πρόβατόν σου καὶ τὸ ὑποζύγιόν σου· ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας ἔσται ὑπὸ τὴν μητέρα, τῇ δὲ ὀγδόῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἀποδώσεις μοι αὐτό. —
hint: Firstborn calves, sheep and beasts of burden stay seven days with the mother and are given on the eighth.

notes.text: The calf, the sheep, the beast of burden: the Hebrew has lĕšōrĕkā lĕṣōʾnekā, your ox and your flock.
ὄγδοος, eighth, one translation, plain text.

reading: [[in this way|in this way, in this manner, so, thus, even so, so much|οὕτως]] [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will produce, you will create|ποιέω]] [[the calf|the calf, the young bull, the heifer and young cow, the boy and girl and maid, the young animal|μόσχος]] of you and [[the thing that walks forward|the thing that walks forward, the cattle, the flocks and herds, the horses, the small cattle, the sheep|πρόβατον]] of you and [[the beast for the yoke|the beast for the yoke and beast of burden|ὑποζύγιον]] of you; seven [[days|days, day-breaks, times|ἡμέρα]] will be [[towards and under|towards and under, under and into, under and before, under, in subjection, towards, about, about the time, to a certain degree and in some measure|ὑπό + accusative]] [[the mother|the mother, the dam, the source|μήτηρ]], [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], to the eighth [[to day|to day, to day-break, to time|ἡμέρα]] [[you will give up|you will give up, you will give back, you will restore, you will return, you will render what is due and pay, you will return and render and yield, you will suffer and allow, you will render, you will deliver over and give up, you will deliver, you will render and give in, you will give an account of, you will increase|ἀποδίδωμι]] to me it. —

greek: καὶ ἄνδρες ἅγιοι ἔσεσθέ μοι. καὶ κρέας θηριάλωτον οὐκ ἔδεσθε, τῷ κυνὶ ἀπορρίψατε αὐτό.
hint: Israel is to be holy; meat torn by wild beasts is not eaten but thrown to the dogs.

notes.text: ἀπορρίπτω, to throw away, the aorist imperative; its to shoot forth bold, keen words is restored whole.
To the dog, singular, for the Hebrew lakkeleb.

reading: and [[men|men, men in the prime of life|ἀνήρ]] [[devoted to the gods|devoted to the gods and sacred and holy, holy and pure|ἅγιος]] you will be to me. and [[flesh|flesh and meat and a piece of meat, dressed meat, a body and person|κρέας]] caught by wild beasts not [[you will eat|you will eat, you will eat of|ἐσθίω]], [[to the dog|to the dog and bitch, to the hounds, to the shamelessness, to the audacity, to the rashness and recklessness, to the sea-dog, to the dog-star, to the dog of Orion|κύων]] [[throw away|throw away and put away, cast forth, disown and renounce, throw aside and set at naught, shoot forth bold and keen words, let fall|ἀπορρίπτω]] it.
